ambiguities.evidence: Equation (3.20) has no explicit u_m factor and Remark 4 says it removes dependence on u_m, but Theorem 3.4 still assumes condition (3.16), which contains u_m eta_R kappa(M_R), and rho_A^R is built from vectors computed by fl(M_R^-1 hat_v_j) in precision u_m (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchors: equations (3.14)-(3.16); PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, anchors: equation (3.20) and Remark 4).
ambiguities.impact: The safest reading is that flexible solution formation removes the explicit reapplication contribution from the envelope; it does not make theorem applicability or all computed intermediate quantities mathematically independent of u_m.
ambiguities.issue: Remark 4's removal-of-u_m language is broader than the literal theorem statement.

ambiguities.evidence: Section 3.5 reports rho_A^R behaving like c(n,k) in the main experiments but also mentions extreme unreported cases where it was of order kappa(M_R), and says further investigation is needed (PDF p. 13, printed p. 12, anchor: rho_A^R simplification bullet).
ambiguities.impact: Replacing rho_A^R by an order-one constant, or claiming complete u_m insensitivity through it, belongs only to the simplified or empirical discussion and not to the original theorem.
ambiguities.issue: The magnitude and possible precision dependence of rho_A^R are not theoretically resolved.

ambiguities.evidence: Remark 3 says the u_a kappa(A M_R^-1)kappa(M_R) requirement is likely pessimistic and offers condition (3.18) involving tilde_Z_k; Remark 5 says the corresponding requirement and u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) are likely pessimistic for the flexible theorem (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 10-11, anchors: Remarks 3 and 5).
ambiguities.impact: The displayed theorems remain conditional on (3.16), while informal discussion may ignore those conditions; a formal contract must not silently drop them.
ambiguities.issue: Some applicability requirements are explicitly described as likely pessimistic.

ambiguities.evidence: Section 2 defines several normwise condition numbers and then permits the generic notation kappa (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, anchor: condition-number notation); equations (3.16), (3.17), and (3.20) use generic kappa (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 10-11).
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must either retain an abstract condition-number convention or select the appropriate 2-norm/Frobenius variant explicitly.
ambiguities.issue: The exact condition-number norm is abbreviated.

ambiguities.evidence: Algorithm 1 forms x_k from x_0 plus a Krylov correction, while Algorithm 2 line 4 writes x_k = tilde_Z_k y_k and the theorem passages do not restate how x_0 is absorbed (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, anchor: Algorithm 1 lines 17-18; PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, anchor: Algorithm 2 line 4).
ambiguities.impact: The source formulas clearly govern the analyzed computed approximation, but a literal algorithm-level formalization should specify whether x_0 = 0 or whether the analyzed system is the correction system.
ambiguities.issue: Algorithm 1 displays an initial guess x_0, whereas modular Algorithm 2 writes the approximation simply as tilde_Z_k y_k.

contract_plain_english: Under the complete smallness condition (3.16), right-preconditioned GMRES attains at some k <= n a first-order forward-error envelope with three sources: ordinary GMRES rounding, a fresh low-precision right-preconditioner application during solution formation, and multiplication by A. Flexible-preconditioned GMRES stores the already preconditioned basis and therefore has the same conditional envelope with the middle term u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) removed. This is a proved difference in the displayed bounds, but the flexible theorem still retains u_m in its applicability condition and may retain implicit u_m effects through its computed basis and rho_A^R. Experiments support improved flexible robustness when preconditioner precision is lowered, while also showing increased iteration counts and some real-problem outliers (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 10-11, anchors: equations (3.16), (3.17), (3.20), and Remark 4; PDF pp. 20-21 and 32, printed pp. 19-20 and 31, anchors: Sections 4.2.3 and 5.1).

source_evidence.anchor: Algorithm 1, right-preconditioned variant and surrounding text
source_evidence.observation: Right-preconditioned MGS-GMRES applies M_R^-1 to hat_v_j in precision u_m, applies A in precision u_a, performs the remaining GMRES operations in precision u_g, and at solution formation computes hat_V_k hat_y_k before reapplying M_R^-1. Flexible-preconditioning instead stores the vectors z_j and forms the solution from Z_k y_k.

The preconditioner model is fl(M_R^-1 hat_v_j) = (M_R^-1 + Delta M_R^(j))hat_v_j with normF(Delta M_R^(j)) <= c(n,k)u_m eta_R normF(M_R^-1). rho_A^R is defined by (3.15). Under the five-term smallness condition (3.16), there exists k <= n satisfying the right-preconditioned forward-error bound (3.17).
The condition is max{u_g kappa(A M_R^-1), u_g kappa(M_R), u_m eta_R kappa(M_R), u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R, u_a kappa(A M_R^-1)kappa(M_R)} << 1.

Flexible-preconditioned GMRES uses a fixed M_R^(j) = M_R != I, stores hat_Z_k explicitly, and forms the approximation directly by a standard matrix-vector product with hat_Z_k in precision u_g without reapplying M_R^-1. Assuming (3.16), there exists k <= n satisfying bound (3.20), whose right-hand side omits u_m eta_R kappa(M_R).

Remark 4 attributes removal of u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) to avoiding reapplication of M_R^-1 and says this removes dependence on precision u_m. Remark 5 nevertheless says the u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) and u_a kappa(A M_R^-1)kappa(M_R) requirements retained through condition (3.16) are likely pessimistic.

After heuristically assuming eta_R and rho_A^R are order-constant, ignoring c(n,k), and ignoring the applicability conditions, the paper simplifies the right bound to u_g kappa(A M_R^-1)kappa(M_R) + u_m kappa(M_R) + u_a kappa(A), and the flexible bound to u_g kappa(A M_R^-1)kappa(M_R) + u_a kappa(A). It reports observed order-constant rho_A^R in its main experiments but also unreported extreme non-practical cases where rho_A^R was of order kappa(M_R).

For flexible-preconditioning, hat_x_k = fl(hat_Z_k hat_y_k) and the solution-formation perturbation satisfies norm2(Delta x) <= c(n,k)[u_g kappa(M_R) + u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R]norm2(tilde_Z_k hat_y_k). Comparing this with (C.11), the proof explicitly identifies the absent reapplication term.

source_evidence.anchor: Appendix D, closing recovery of equation (3.20)
source_evidence.observation: The proof substitutes the new epsilon_x into the modular bound and states that it recovers forward-error bound (3.20).
In synthetic experiments for u_a = u_g << u_m, lowering preconditioner precision leaves flexible variants' observed robustness unchanged but significantly increases their iteration counts.

For right-preconditioning, the paper reports the additional u_m kappa(M_R) term becoming dominant in the low-preconditioner-precision strategy and observes reduced robustness, while noting that right-preconditioning uses less basis storage than flexible-preconditioning.

On SuiteSparse experiments, flexible-preconditioning usually has better robustness and iteration counts for the low-preconditioner-precision variants, but the paper explicitly records outliers and a more nuanced comparison between right and left preconditioning.

statement.algorithm_linkage: Both variants compute hat_z_j = fl(M_R^-1 hat_v_j) and Ahat_z_j during basis construction. Right-preconditioned GMRES later computes hat_V_k hat_y_k and applies M_R^-1 again, whereas flexible-preconditioned GMRES stores hat_Z_k and computes hat_Z_k hat_y_k directly; the removed final reapplication is the source of the missing u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) term (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, anchor: Algorithm 1 and flexible modification; PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 10-11, anchors: Sections 3.3-3.4 and Remark 4).
binders: Let A in R^(n x n) be nonsingular, let 0 != b in R^n, and let M_R in R^(n x n) be a nonsingular right preconditioner with M_L = I; the sections consider M_R != I (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1, anchor: equation (1.1); PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: opening of Section 3.3).

Let u_a, u_m, and u_g be the unit roundoffs for multiplication by A, application of M_R^-1, and the remaining GMRES operations respectively, and let eta_R quantify preconditioner-application error (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, anchor: Algorithm 1; PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.14)).

For j <= k, let hat_z_j = fl(M_R^-1 hat_v_j), hat_Z_k = [hat_z_1,...,hat_z_k], and let hat_y_k be the computed least-squares coefficient vector (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equations (3.14)-(3.15)).
For flexible-preconditioning, M_R^(j) = M_R is fixed for every j <= k, despite the method's ability in general to vary the preconditioner (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, anchor: opening of Section 3.4).
conclusions: For right-preconditioned GMRES, there exists an iteration k <= n such that norm2(hat_x_k - x)/norm2(x) is less than or approximately equal to c(n,k)[u_g kappa(A M_R^-1)kappa(M_R) + u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) + u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R] (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.17)).

For flexible-preconditioned GMRES with fixed M_R, there exists an iteration k <= n such that norm2(hat_x_k - x)/norm2(x) is less than or approximately equal to c(n,k)[u_g kappa(A M_R^-1)kappa(M_R) + u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R] (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, anchor: equation (3.20)).
The explicit difference between the displayed envelopes is precisely the right-preconditioned term u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, anchor: Remark 4).

The paper attributes this difference to flexible-preconditioning's reuse of stored preconditioned vectors rather than a fresh application of M_R^-1 during solution formation (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, anchor: Section 3.4 and Remark 4; PDF p. 44, printed p. 43, anchor: equations (D.1)-(D.2)).
constants_and_indexing: Both conclusions are existential: each asserts some k <= n, not all k and not a prescribed iteration (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 10-11, anchors: Theorems 3.3-3.4).
Flexible-preconditioning uses the same fixed M_R for all j <= k (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, anchor: opening of Section 3.4).
The five quantities inside the maximum in condition (3.16) must all be small (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.16)).
c(n,k) is an unspecified low-degree polynomial and may change between estimates (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, anchor: Section 2 definition of c(n,k)).
definitions_and_conventions: The normalized forward error is norm2(hat_x_k - x)/norm2(x) for the original system Ax = b (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, anchor: equation (2.1); PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 10-11, anchors: equations (3.17) and (3.20)).

eta_R is a scalar measuring the magnitude of error in applying M_R^-1; the original theorems do not set eta_R to one or assume it is constant (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.14) and following sentence).
rho_A^R measures componentwise cancellation in the stored basis product through norm2(|hat_Z_k||hat_y_k|)/norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k) (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.15)).

The later equations (3.22)-(3.23) are simplified discussion bounds obtained only after additional assumptions; they are not the original theorem statements (PDF p. 13, printed p. 12, anchor: Section 3.5 and equations (3.22)-(3.23)).
error_notions: Equations (3.17) and (3.20) bound attainable normalized forward error, not backward error and not residual norm (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 10-11, anchors: Theorems 3.3-3.4; PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, anchor: statement that Section 3 focuses solely on forward error).

The u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) term represents error from reapplying the right preconditioner during right-preconditioned solution formation (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, anchor: Remark 4; PDF p. 43, printed p. 42, anchor: equation (C.11)).

The u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R term captures error from multiplication by A together with componentwise cancellation in the stored basis product (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equations (3.15)-(3.17); PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.7)).
exceptional_values: A and M_R must be nonsingular, and b is nonzero, so x and the displayed normalized forward-error denominator are nonzero (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1, anchor: equation (1.1); PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: Theorem 3.3 and use of M_R^-1).
rho_A^R has denominator norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k); the paper does not explicitly exclude a zero denominator (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.15)).

The standard floating-point model does not explicitly describe overflow, underflow, NaN, or infinity, so the bounds presume ordinary finite modeled operations (PDF p. 5, printed p. 4, anchor: standard floating-point model statement).
higher_order_terms: Both envelopes use the paper's less-than-or-approximately-equal symbol, which denotes omission of negligible second-order terms (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, anchor: approximation convention; PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 10-11, anchors: equations (3.17) and (3.20)).

The simplified envelopes (3.22)-(3.23) additionally discard c(n,k), treat eta_R and rho_A^R as order-constant, and ignore the theorem applicability conditions (PDF p. 13, printed p. 12, anchor: assumptions preceding equations (3.21)-(3.23)).
hypotheses: For every relevant j, fl(M_R^-1 hat_v_j) = (M_R^-1 + Delta M_R^(j))hat_v_j and normF(Delta M_R^(j)) <= c(n,k)u_m eta_R normF(M_R^-1) (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.14)).
rho_A^R = norm2(|hat_Z_k||hat_y_k|)/norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k) (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.15)).

The full condition max{u_g kappa(A M_R^-1), u_g kappa(M_R), u_m eta_R kappa(M_R), u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R, u_a kappa(A M_R^-1)kappa(M_R)} << 1 is assumed for both Theorems 3.3 and 3.4 (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.16); PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, anchor: Theorem 3.4).

Right-preconditioned solution formation multiplies by hat_V_k in precision u_g and then reapplies M_R^-1 in precision u_m; flexible solution formation multiplies directly by the stored hat_Z_k in precision u_g (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: paragraph preceding equation (3.15); PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, anchor: paragraphs preceding Theorem 3.4).
implicit_context: With fixed M_R, right- and flexible-preconditioned GMRES are mathematically equivalent in exact arithmetic, but their different solution-formation paths produce different rounding-error bounds (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, anchor: text following Algorithm 1; PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, anchor: opening of Section 3.4).

The bounds are worst-case attainable-error results and do not provide a convergence-rate guarantee or a bound at every iteration (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, anchor: opening of Section 3; PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 10-11, anchors: Theorems 3.3-3.4).

Synthetic experiments support robustness insensitivity of flexible-preconditioning to lower u_m but also show significantly more iterations, so omission of the u_m term is not a claim of unchanged convergence rate or runtime (PDF p. 20, printed p. 19, anchor: Section 4.2.3 flexible-preconditioned discussion).

Real-life experiments generally favor flexible-preconditioning for low-precision preconditioner application but contain explicit outliers, so the empirical preference is not universal (PDF p. 32, printed p. 31, anchor: Section 5.1 discussion following Table 5).
norms: The forward errors and rho_A^R use vector 2-norms (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 10-11, anchors: equations (3.15), (3.17), and (3.20)).
The preconditioner perturbation model uses the Frobenius matrix norm (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.14)).

The condition numbers are written with generic kappa; Section 2 permits this abbreviation among its 2-norm/Frobenius-based condition measures (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, anchor: condition-number notation).
numerical_model: Applications of M_R^-1 are modeled by normwise matrix perturbations proportional to c(n,k)u_m eta_R, while products with A are performed in precision u_a and other GMRES operations in precision u_g (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, anchor: Algorithm 1; PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.14)).

Right solution formation incurs a fresh preconditioner-application perturbation; flexible solution formation instead has the standard product model hat_x_k = fl(hat_Z_k hat_y_k) = (hat_Z_k + Delta Z_k^(3))hat_y_k with |Delta Z_k^(3)| bounded by c(n,k)u_g|hat_Z_k| (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.3); PDF p. 44, printed p. 43, anchor: equation (D.1)).

The paper adopts a traditional worst-case floating-point analysis and does not track exact values of all dimension-dependent constants (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, anchor: Section 2 definition of c(n,k)).

undebatable_constraints: The right envelope contains all three terms u_g kappa(A M_R^-1)kappa(M_R), u_m eta_R kappa(M_R), and u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.17)).
The flexible envelope contains the first and third of those terms but not u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, anchor: equation (3.20)).
Both theorem statements assume the same condition (3.16), including its explicit u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) requirement (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 10-11, anchors: condition (3.16) and Theorem 3.4).

The missing term is linked specifically to avoiding reapplication of M_R^-1 during solution formation, not to eliminating preconditioner applications during Krylov-basis construction (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, anchor: Section 3.4 and Remark 4).
The flexible theorem assumes a fixed preconditioner M_R^(j) = M_R for all j <= k (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, anchor: opening of Section 3.4).

The envelopes are conditional, first-order, existential attainable-forward-error claims; they are not unconditional convergence or runtime claims (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 10-11, anchors: Theorems 3.3-3.4; PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, anchor: approximation convention).
